_readme: State irrigation project register, transcribed verbatim from the Government of Andhra Pradesh's Socio-Economic Survey editions 2017-18, 2018-19, 2020-21, 2021-22 and 2024-25 (the editions on hand that print a project-wise table or status prose; 2019-20 and 2022-23 print none — honest gaps). AP publishes no online project register, so the SES is the government's own recurring project-wise record. Figures are kept exactly as printed, including percentages that move backwards between editions and targets that slip; disagreements are never reconciled. Costs are the printed admin approvals/sanctions (mostly SES 2018-19, the last edition to print them). Observation dates follow each edition's stated cutoff (see source labels); the tables themselves print no as-on date. Eye-checked against rendered page images on 2026-09-02. Load with: python scripts/load_state_projects.py

projects.title: Poola Subbaiah Veligonda Project
projects.department: Water Resources Department, Government of Andhra Pradesh
projects.description: Veligonda — flood-water diversion of 43.50 TMC from the Krishna (Kollam Vagu/Srisailam foreshore) by gravity to the drought-prone, fluoride-affected uplands of Prakasam, Nellore and Kadapa districts (30 mandals); contemplated irrigation for about 4.47 lakh acres and drinking water for 15.25 lakh people. The government's own record moves backwards: SES 2017-18 says 'Overall, 81% work is completed… entire project by December 2018'; SES 2018-19 prints 74% (admin approval Rs 6,017.99 Cr, target 12/2020); SES 2020-21 and 2021-22 print 78% (target 2023); SES 2024-25 prints 75% (target 2026). Each figure is kept exactly as printed. On 1 September 2026 the Chief Minister inaugurated Phase-1 at Gantavanipalli (Prakasam), releasing water from the 18.8 km twin tunnels into the 21.8 km feeder canal towards Nallamala Sagar; press reports put Phase-1 at 19,000 acres and drinking water for about 4 lakh people, with Rs 5,662 crore spent against a project cost reported as 'over Rs 10,200 crore' (The Hans India, 1-2 Sep 2026 — press figures, no government order on record yet). The project as a whole remains ongoing.
